devices.name: Magic Leap 1 and 2
devices.role: Senior Director, Spatial AR Platform & Applications
devices.imageNote: Same still as video.html: Test Driving Magic Leap's AR Goggles

bullets: Senior Director managing a 30-engineer international team through the Magic Leap 1 and 2 launches. Leads and architects reported to him.
Staff grew 10% during a company-wide 50% reduction, with delivery continuing through that period.
Launched flagship Spatial AR Meetings (personas, collaboration, and laptop interop) within a year of prototyping.
Shipped the first generation of Magic Leap applications: Avatars, Media player, and Mobile Companion app, including synchronized multidevice shared spatial interactions on a VPS map.
Designed and built foundational C++ frameworks and APIs for multi-headset collaboration, with real-time 3D graphics streaming from mobile and desktop companions.
Debugged the wireless controller firmware and driver stack and identified design flaws that caused intermittent behavior.
Engineered a 1000x performance improvement for applications on the pre-V1 Magic Leap AR platform, and designed multi-application shared spatial context and device-to-cloud-to-device sharing APIs.
Led performance investigations into Android (AOSP) native ports, including graphics, DASH video, and gesture interactions.

devices.name: DAQRI XR Smart Helmet
devices.role: Director of Engineering; Chief Software Architect & Lead
devices.imageNote: Same still as video.html: DAQRI Smart Helmet — Hands On

bullets: Director of Engineering for a 70-person org. Leads and architects reported to him. Led the full software stack, from the firmware for the cameras and sensors up to the cloud.
Launched the XR Smart Helmet, an industrial AR hard hat with depth and thermal sensing. It was shown during Intel CEO Brian Krzanich's CES 2016 keynote.

Managed a 45-engineer team to deliver 15+ customer apps and 2 releases of the core spatial frameworks in 9 months. Owned staffing, architecture, strategy planning, budgeting, recruiting oversight, and executive communication.
As Chief Software Architect, managed the software team as it grew from 3 to 30 engineers.
Built a fleet management dashboard to reduce overall cost and improve reliability across the device fleet.
Advised on the sensor-fusion firmware code to fix problems with globally synchronized timestamps.

Created the Unity/C# spatial framework API for industrial and factory AR UI: latency-critical info panels, workflow data, and head-relative, body-relative, and world-placed panels, plus status panels, a camera with photo log, task checklists, digital gauges, barcode scanners, and proximity alerts.
Led architecture design for the XR helmet in industrial settings so spatial computing could support factory and field operations.

devices.name: Kinect for Windows and Xbox One
devices.role: Senior Software Development Engineer, Xbox One and Windows Kinect
devices.imageNote: Same still as video.html: Kinect for Windows v2 — Color, Depth, IR & Body Streams

bullets: Developed body-tracking spatial interactions and an API in C++, shipped in Windows and Xbox. Designed a migration from heuristics to reinforcement learning.

Created the developer-facing Kinect framework from researcher prototype code. Designed a latency-critical multithreaded architecture to launch Kinect on Windows in 64-bit mode, and skeletal tracking debugging tools for recording and playback of gestures.
Created a spatial UI API for latency-critical UI controlled by hand motion. Delivered an NUI interaction described as more natural that let users complete tests in 80% less time.
Xbox One Kinect user interactions: developed interpretation of body movements into interactions with on-screen interfaces.

Ergonomic Physical Interaction Zone Cursor Mapping (US 9,063,578, 2015) maps physical hand-movement zones to cursor motion for motion controllers or touchless sensors. The PHIZ mockup is linked below.

devices.name: Clarion AutoPC and Windows Automotive car stereos
devices.role: AutoPC UI frameworks; later Engineering Manager & Architect, Automotive Platform

bullets: Later automotive platform: Engineering Manager and Architect. Managed a 15-engineer international team and merged the Redmond and Japan development groups into one team.

Deliveries of the developer-facing automotive UI/HMI APIs included Ford Sync, BMW, Citroën, DaimlerChrysler, Fiat, Honda, Hyundai, Kia, Nissan, Toyota, and Volvo. Shipped 3 CTP releases to customers in 2009 and guided technical negotiations with customers in Japan.

bullets.text: Clarion AutoPC (1998–2002) is recorded as individual-contributor UI framework work. Org leadership for that product is not in the resume. Confirm with Richard.

bullets: Clarion AutoPC: created the developer-facing UI frameworks API for automotive HMI (infotainment) in C++, MFC, and ARM. The framework had rich interaction controls, customizable themes, and multi-modal interactions including embedded speech-controlled devices. The resume ties this work to patents on skinnable UI, multi-modal interactions, and embedded speech-controlled devices.

Later Windows Automotive platform: led delivery of UI/HMI frameworks with a native C++ extension for XAML, including hardware 2D and 3D acceleration, aimed at ARM-based car stereos. The project record names global partners including BMW, Ford, and Toyota.

Evaluated WPF, Silverlight, and Media Center XAML for ARM-based car stereos, then created a Windows Automotive XAML solution from Silverlight's lightness with a C++ interface and 3D features, avoiding C# runtime overhead.
Kindle developer API architecture: defined application UI APIs enabling e-paper interactions for launch experiences on the Kindle e-reader.

Book page service alongside that launch work: proposed and created a petabyte-scale, low-latency web service for 900,000 book-page images, reducing delivery time by 30%. Served 220 million images (90+ terabytes) worldwide, with caching for Europe, Asia, and the Americas.

Investigated developer challenges and built solutions for the Xbox Advanced Technology Group to streamline the developer experience. The project record tags that work as C++, SDK design, and low-level optimization.
